description: Authored campaign-scale route constraints, not a surveyed reconstruction of ancient crossings.

forest.name: Woodland
forest.description: Tree cover conceals approaches; scouts report nearby forces.

hills.name: High ground
hills.description: Defenders hold elevated ground; columns follow the lower tracks.

mountains.name: Mountain country
mountains.description: Armies use marked passes. Unbroken ridges cannot be crossed.

marsh.name: Marshland
marsh.description: Soft ground costs twice a plain march before road improvements.

desert.name: Dry country
desert.description: Loose ground and long approaches slow the column.

steppe.name: Open steppe
steppe.description: Open grassland favors movement and mounted reconnaissance.

bridge.name: Bridge crossing
bridge.description: The road crosses the river at a bridge. Defenders control the narrow approach.

river.name: Unbridged river
river.description: No land crossing here. Find a bridge on another route.

causeway.name: Marsh causeway
causeway.description: A raised crossing concentrates troops onto a narrow approach.

pass.name: Mountain pass
pass.description: The pass is traversable; the surrounding ridge is not.

ridge.name: Unbroken ridge
ridge.description: No traversable pass on this border. Route around the ridge.

water.name: Open water
water.description: Land armies cannot march across this water. Use coastal transport.
